feedback_rules.description: Ensure the shoulder cloth is held firmly at both ends and propelled in coordination with the directional steps; a camera cannot verify internal devotional intent or fasting discipline.

learning_units.description: Mastering the Parva cloth movement: holding the ends of a shoulder cloth in both hands and extending it forward and backward to the rhythm.
Lateral coordination: moving the cloth and stepping right and left to the rhythmic accompaniment of the dhol and mahuri.

prerequisites.description: Adequate physical stamina to perform repetitive grounded stepping and arm extension while wearing costume frames.

social_formats.description: Sequential male duet and group character roles (Prabhakar/Prabhakariani, Fakir/Fakiriani, Savara/Savarani) performed in community spaces accompanied by Ghasi drummers and pipers.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Both hands grasp the ends of a cloth draped around the neck and shoulders, extending and retracting forward, backward, and side-to-side.
movement_profile.footwork: Rhythmic stepping moving forward, backward, left, and right coordinated with cloth manipulations.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Duet staging in open village spaces, facing each other for dramatic dialogues or circling within community arenas.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Lateral swaying and torso direction changes aligning with character portrayal in theatrical vignettes.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Primarily grounded footwork; acrobatic and ascetic physical austerities performed during daylight ritual phases.
movement_profile.partnering: Structured duets between complementary character archetypes (e.g., Prabhakar and Prabhakariani, Fakir and Fakiriani, Savara and Savarani).
movement_profile.posture: Erect and grounded posture, often bearing back-mounted bamboo ornamental frames or ritual props.

signature_moves.description: Holding both ends of a shoulder-draped cloth and moving it rhythmically forward, backward, left, and right.
signature_moves.name: Parva Vastra Chalana

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Casual reenactment of sacred ritual penances; omitting the respectful dramatic conventions of character duets.

music_profile.musical_form: Sequential character vignettes and leela narratives featuring alternating question-and-answer dialogue songs.
music_profile.sound_description: The sonic signature is driven by the sharp, percussive strokes of the dhol drum accompanying the shrill, nasal melodic phrases of the mahuri wind pipe, intercut with expressive folk-Odissi singing.
music_profile.vocal_style: Dramatic, devotional, dialogic question-and-answer, blending folk singing with Odissi vocal stylings.

basic_steps: Stand balanced holding the ends of a shoulder cloth in both hands.
Step rhythmically forward while pushing the cloth outward in time with the dhol.
Step backward while drawing the cloth back toward the chest.
Shift weight to the right side while tilting and gesturing with the cloth.
Shift weight to the left side in coordination with the mahuri melody.
teaching.formation: Duet pairings and processional village arena presentations
teaching.level_notes: Beginners learn the basic Parva cloth-manipulation patterns and rhythmic step matching before moving to specialized dramatic dialogues.
teaching.rhythm: Dynamic folk and Odissi meters punctuated by dhol beats
